_comment: OHAO golden-image regression corpus. Run from repo root.
_what_this_gate_actually_is: Read this before trusting a green run, and before loosening anything.
These scenes are Monte Carlo path traces. The renderer is deterministic for
a fixed sampler and a fixed build -- two runs are byte-identical -- so this
corpus is, in practice, a HASH of an unchanged sampler with enough slack for
the GPU floating-point floor. It is not a tolerance gate in the sense of
'the image is still about right', and it cannot be made into one by raising
the sample count. Measured on cornell_box against a 1024 spp reference:
16 spp is max_abs 88 / rmse 10.8, 64 spp is 47 / 6.9, 256 spp is 34 / 4.1.
Noise falls as 1/sqrt(N), so a max_abs 4 tolerance is out of reach at any
sample count anyone will wait for.
WHAT IT CATCHES: a changed shader, a changed material, a broken pass, a
missing asset -- anything that moves pixels while the sample sequence stays
put. That is the common case and the gate is genuinely good at it.
WHAT IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH: a real regression from any change that perturbs
the sample SEQUENCE (a new sampler dimension, a reordered bounce, a changed
seed). Both reshuffle every pixel by the noise magnitude. When you change
sampling, this corpus will go red and it cannot tell you whether you also
broke something. Verify that case by eye or with a converged render.
Exact where exactness is achievable (sub-project 2b step 5): the deferred
scenes render one pixel hash in every fresh process (max_abs 0). The
path-traced scenes keep a measured floor of 1 LSB on a few pixels: the
driver's BLAS builder lays out the BVH differently run to run (identical
input, different serialized bytes), and a ray that hits exactly on an edge
two triangles share takes whichever one the traversal reaches first. Every
mesh has such edges (Cornell's walls are two-triangle quads). Their tolerance
is that floor, 1 / 0.0005, not noise.
_growing: Denoiser OFF on every scene: we pin raw deterministic beauty. A denoiser is a large, version-dependent, non-linear prior, and pinning its output pins the denoiser rather than the renderer.
Grow this list as features land -- every fixed bug should add a scene so it cannot silently regress. A scene costs one entry here and a few seconds a run.

A scene must load only TRACKED assets, or it is not a gate on a fresh clone. Not a style rule: the scene this replaced pointed at a file nobody had, and its empty render was reported as a pixel regression for two months.
_regenerating: It overwrites without comparing, so it cannot tell an intentional refresh
from laundering a regression. Look at what drifted FIRST. The goldens these
replaced were 78 renderer commits stale and nobody knew, because the harness
could not run at all on a multi-config generator.

scenes.name: cornell_box
scenes._note: Builds its scene in code and loads no asset, so it runs on a bare clone. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 4): the path tracer applies an untextured material's base color once (a legacy 1x1 tint texture applied it a second time); brighter, max_abs 70 on 100% of pixels. Tightened in 2b step 5 (was 4 / 0.01) to the BVH floor (see _what_this_gate_actually_is): 24 fresh-process renders gave one pixel hash, and no Cornell render flipped run to run in 78; the ohao CLI's twin, whose scene loads from the file in another order and so builds another BVH, can differ from this example's golden on a few pixels by 1.

scenes.name: damaged_helmet
scenes._note: Tightened in 2b step 5 (was 4 / 0.01) to its measured floor: 1 LSB on at most 12 fixed full-resolution pixels in a minority of runs (5 of 83 fresh-process renders, 3 of them the first run after a shader rebuild; 3-4 compare-resolution pixels at max_abs 1), from the driver's run-to-run BVH layout deciding edge hits (see _what_this_gate_actually_is). Replaces metal_rough_spheres, whose MetalRoughSpheres.glb was never in the repository. model_viewer used to exit 0 after a failed load and render an empty frame, so that scene reported a large pixel difference for two months instead of a missing file. DamagedHelmet.glb IS tracked (3.7 MB) and covers the same ground: a metal/rough glTF under an HDRI. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 3): glTF node transforms now reach the vertices, so the helmet stands upright (it lay on its back), and the framer backs the camera off to z 30.53 so the upright helmet fits the frame; the whole image changes (max_abs 221-244 on 95-100% of pixels against the old golden), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 4): the room's untextured materials take their base color once (a legacy 1x1 tint texture applied it a second time); brighter walls, max_abs 91 on 99.8% of pixels.
scenes._recaptured: 2026-10-10, sub-project 2a Task 8 (RT reads RenderScene). The old golden was NOT lit by the HDRI: the legacy RT build loaded the env map before any path tracer existed, so it took bindless index 0 -- the first wall's 1x1 solid-color layer -- and every miss ray returned that constant color. The new path registers the HDRI in the one texture table. Verified at 1024 spp against master: with the old index emulated, master vs new is max_abs 9 / frac>4 0.0002 inside the helmet box and 8 / 0.0001 outside (640-wide); with the real HDRI the whole frame changes (mean RGB 130 -> 98). Albedo/emissive textures are now sRGB-decoded by the sampler instead of pow(2.2) on UNORM; the helmet's textures were already sampled at their native 2048^2.

scenes.name: cornell_box_deferred
scenes._note: Deferred hybrid (G-buffer + RT shadows/GI where supported). Captured on master before sub-project 2a so the ECS/RenderScene migration is checked against the old renderer's own output. Exact since sub-project 4 step 1 (2026-10-23): deferred rendering is bit-identical run to run, ten separate-process renders gave one pixel hash, and this golden has measured max_abs 0 in every session since 2026-10-09. Any difference is a change to look at, not noise. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 2): the example now writes the last of its 10 frames, not frame 7 from the deleted headless readback ring; frame 10 vs 7 is max_abs 3 on 36.8% of pixels, RT GI's history three frames further on, and equals `ohao run --frames 10` bit for bit. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 4): RT shadows trace the scene's ceiling light instead of a hard-coded point at (0, 4.5, 0); max_abs 2 on 0.9% of pixels. Re-captured again (2b step 4): RT shadow and GI rays seeded by (render seed, frame since reset, pixel, sample); scattered noise, max_abs 3 on 39.8% of pixels. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (2b step 7): RT shadows rebuilt (one ray to each of a pixel's 4 most important lights, a 5x5 filter and a temporal accumulation, visibility in 8 bits a light); Cornell's dim lights barely shadow, max_abs 1 on a few pixels. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (2b step 8): RT GI rebuilt (half resolution, 2 rays a pixel, temporal accumulation, 2 a-trous iterations, joint-bilateral upsample; a bounce lit by the 4 brightest lights with the lighting pass's attenuation and 1/pi); the indirect light is smoother and a little dimmer, max_abs 21 on 80.0% of pixels, looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (2b step 9): SSS runs only on materials with `subsurface` (the old albedo heuristic took the red wall for skin and blurred it over the ceiling edge), and SSR is traced at half resolution; max_abs 34 on 4.5% of pixels, the red wall's edge sharp again, looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (environment reflections): the deferred frame's environment light is split-sum IBL from a GGX-prefiltered environment (6 levels, read at the pixel's roughness) and a cosine-convolved irradiance image, scaled by the environment's intensity, weighted by RT GI's environment visibility (the fraction of GI rays that leave the scene) with GI's bounce radiance for the occluded rest, and occluded by material AO and SSAO through a specular-occlusion term; the unprefiltered mip-0 lookup, the 1x1 BRDF-LUT fallback and the metal ambient floor are gone. Cornell has no environment: only the GI denoiser now carrying raw radiance changes it, max_abs 1 on 0.2% of pixels, looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (SSR composition): screen-space reflections replace the environment/GI reflection where their trace hits instead of being added on top of it in tonemapping (lighting writes its environment specular E and reflection weight W, the split sum with specular occlusion, and SSR's resolve does lit += W*(c*L) - c*E before bloom and TAA, so reflected light is counted once and under one weight), and the constant ambient term is diffuse only (albedo * (1 - metallic): on metals it was a flat F0-tinted glow the path tracer has no counterpart for). The two mirror spheres lose the grey ambient wash and reflect the red and green walls at their sides and the open front (black) at their centre, as the path-traced cornell_box does; max_abs 147 on 2.7% of pixels (rmse 19.5), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-26 (ambient kill): the constant ambient (0.35 x diffuse albedo, on every surface on top of RT GI) is now only the fallback of a frame with neither RT GI nor an environment; with RT GI the walls are lit by direct light and its one bounce only, as in the path tracer, which has no such term. The whole frame darkens where it was flat-filled. Back wall 0.581 -> 0.360 mean luma (path tracer 0.330), red wall 0.138 -> 0.085, green 0.239 -> 0.125; light now falls off toward the floor and the walls bleed colour onto each other; max_abs 151 on 98.8% of pixels (rmse 52.7), looked at before the update.

scenes.name: damaged_helmet_deferred
scenes._note: Deferred hybrid on the helmet with TAA, SSAO and bloom; same purpose as cornell_box_deferred. Exact since sub-project 4 step 1 (2026-10-23). It used to move run to run (max_abs 1-5, ~2.6% of pixels) because bloom's mip chain read each mip before the previous render pass's writes were visible, and TAA's first frame read an unset previous view-projection; both are fixed, ten separate-process renders gave one pixel hash, and the golden was regenerated then (the old one differed by max_abs 1 on 2.9% of pixels, scattered: one sample of the race). Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 2): model_viewer now writes the last of its 30 frames, not frame 27 from the deleted headless readback ring; frame 30 vs 27 is max_abs 9 on 39.4% of pixels, scattered few-LSB noise of the RT GI and TAA histories converging, and equals `ohao run --frames 30` bit for bit. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 3): glTF node transforms now reach the vertices, so the helmet stands upright (it lay on its back), and the framer backs the camera off to z 30.53 so the upright helmet fits the frame; the whole image changes (max_abs 221-244 on 95-100% of pixels against the old golden), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 4): RT shadows trace the room's four lights, each into its own mask channel, instead of one hard-coded point light darkening all of them; highlights the old mask hid reappear (max_abs 84 on 6.9% of pixels). Re-captured again (2b step 4): RT shadow and GI rays seeded by (render seed, frame since reset, pixel, sample); scattered noise, max_abs 18 on 59.0% of pixels. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (2b step 7): RT shadows rebuilt (one ray to each of a pixel's 4 most important lights, filtered and accumulated over the 30 frames); the shelf's penumbra on the box top and scattered 1-LSB noise, max_abs 16 on 2.2% of pixels, looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (2b step 8): RT GI rebuilt (half resolution, 2 rays, denoised), and the environment's diffuse light now arrives through GI rays that leave the room (occluded) instead of the lighting pass's unoccluded IBL term; walls and floor greyer, max_abs 82 on 95.2% of pixels, looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (2b step 9): SSAO applied for the first time (half resolution, to the ambient and IBL terms only), SSR at half resolution, SSS only on `subsurface` materials (the albedo heuristic had blurred reddish parts of the helmet); max_abs 65 on 29.3% of pixels, along edges and in the room's corners, looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (Khronos validation pack): AO comes only from glTF's occlusionTexture; the G-buffer used to read it from the metallicRoughness map's R channel, which is 0.9/255 on average for this helmet, so AO was about 0 and the helmet took no ambient or IBL light at all (its old dark look). With its real occlusion map (mean 0.88) the helmet takes IBL, and the deferred frame's specular IBL is neither occluded nor prefiltered by roughness (one mip level), so its metal mirrors the bright studio HDR and reads as white chrome inside the closed room; the path-traced golden shows what it should approach. max_abs 251 on 37.1% of pixels (rmse 66.8), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (environment reflections): the deferred frame's environment light is split-sum IBL from a GGX-prefiltered environment (6 levels, read at the pixel's roughness) and a cosine-convolved irradiance image, scaled by the environment's intensity, weighted by RT GI's environment visibility (the fraction of GI rays that leave the scene) with GI's bounce radiance for the occluded rest, and occluded by material AO and SSAO through a specular-occlusion term; the unprefiltered mip-0 lookup, the 1x1 BRDF-LUT fallback and the metal ambient floor are gone. The helmet's metal no longer mirrors the studio HDR inside the closed room: it reads as dark, rough teal metal, its brightness against the left wall 0.69 (path tracer 0.48, the white-chrome golden 0.90); max_abs 221 on 96.7% of pixels (rmse 82.7), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (SSR composition): screen-space reflections replace the environment/GI reflection where their trace hits instead of being added on top of it in tonemapping (lighting writes its environment specular E and reflection weight W, the split sum with specular occlusion, and SSR's resolve does lit += W*(c*L) - c*E before bloom and TAA, so reflected light is counted once and under one weight), and the constant ambient term is diffuse only (albedo * (1 - metallic): on metals it was a flat F0-tinted glow the path tracer has no counterpart for). The helmet's frame reads as dark grey metal instead of bright silver; helmet/left-wall brightness 0.472 (path tracer 0.534, the previous golden 0.734 on the same measure); max_abs 186 on 23.6% of pixels (rmse 22.9), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-26 (ambient kill): the constant ambient (0.35 x diffuse albedo, on every surface on top of RT GI) is now only the fallback of a frame with neither RT GI nor an environment; with RT GI the walls are lit by direct light and its one bounce only, as in the path tracer, which has no such term. The whole frame darkens where it was flat-filled. Helmet/left wall 0.535 (path tracer 0.534; 0.472 before), the left wall 0.646 -> 0.523 (path tracer 0.610: one bounce against all of them); RT GI's denoiser noise now shows on the walls; max_abs 157 on 97.1% of pixels (rmse 46.4), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-26 (emissive colour): the G-buffer has an emitted-radiance attachment (the emissive texture times the material's emissive strength, what the path tracer's hit emits) and lighting adds it in its own colour; before, only its luminance was kept and lighting re-tinted it with the albedo, so the helmet's cyan ring and panel lines glowed dim grey. Ring linear luminance 0.062 -> 0.283 (path tracer 0.367), now cyan; helmet/left wall 0.535 -> 0.585 (the ring is inside the helmet box); max_abs 125 on 4.3% of pixels (rmse 6.6), looked at before the update.

scenes.name: cornell_box_rt_realtime
scenes._note: Realtime path tracer (ReSTIR GI reservoirs, temporal history, 16 frames). Added 2026-10-10 after it lost the device and wrote an all-black frame on master and on this branch: bindings 29-35 (reservoirs, spec hit-distance) were never written into the descriptor set. A black frame fails here twice -- the uniform-frame check and max_abs 225. Re-captured 2026-10-24 (sub-project 2b step 4): an untextured material's base color is applied once (a legacy 1x1 tint texture applied it a second time); max_abs 41 on 99.7% of pixels. Tightened in 2b step 5 (was 10 / 0.05) to the BVH floor: the raygen read accumBuffer and normalAOV at neighbour pixels in the dispatch that wrote them, a race (fresh process vs fresh process: max_abs 15-18 on ~43,000 full-resolution channels). The temporal history is now the previous frame's accumulation, a second image (binding 3), and the spatial denoise a compute pass after the trace; 34 example renders gave one pixel hash, and 18 CLI renders another: the CLI's scene, loaded from the file, builds another BVH and renders 10 full-resolution pixels 1 off the example's (one compare pixel). Re-captured then: scattered 1-LSB noise and a few brighter pixels on the sphere's silhouette where the race read half-written neighbours, max_abs 8 on 19.0% of pixels.

scenes.name: khronos_metal_rough_spheres_deferred
scenes._note: Khronos validation pack (2026-10-25, docs/changes/2026-10-25-khronos-validation-pack.md): glTF-Sample-Models MetalRoughSpheres, core metallic-roughness only (base color and metallicRoughness textures, no extensions, no alpha), framed by model_viewer as damaged_helmet is (30 deferred frames, TAA, SSAO and bloom, exposure 1). Exact. Its metallicRoughness map's R channel is 0: the G-buffer used to take AO from it and rendered every sphere black; AO now comes only from glTF's occlusionTexture, which this model has none of. Known, not a regression: the environment has one mip level, so IBL specular does not widen with roughness (the path-traced reference shows the gradient); the two sheets of spheres 8 units apart are in the file. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (environment reflections): the deferred frame's environment light is split-sum IBL from a GGX-prefiltered environment (6 levels, read at the pixel's roughness) and a cosine-convolved irradiance image, scaled by the environment's intensity, weighted by RT GI's environment visibility (the fraction of GI rays that leave the scene) with GI's bounce radiance for the occluded rest, and occluded by material AO and SSAO through a specular-occlusion term; the unprefiltered mip-0 lookup, the 1x1 BRDF-LUT fallback and the metal ambient floor are gone. The known gap this note recorded is fixed: reflections now widen and dim with roughness along each row, as in the path-traced reference; max_abs 240 on 98.3% of pixels (rmse 72.9), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (SSR composition): screen-space reflections replace the environment/GI reflection where their trace hits instead of being added on top of it in tonemapping (lighting writes its environment specular E and reflection weight W, the split sum with specular occlusion, and SSR's resolve does lit += W*(c*L) - c*E before bloom and TAA, so reflected light is counted once and under one weight), and the constant ambient term is diffuse only (albedo * (1 - metallic): on metals it was a flat F0-tinted glow the path tracer has no counterpart for). The metal spheres show reflection contrast instead of a uniform ambient-lit grey, the gold ones saturated gold; max_abs 191 on 29.9% of pixels (rmse 18.9), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-26 (ambient kill): the constant ambient (0.35 x diffuse albedo, on every surface on top of RT GI) is now only the fallback of a frame with neither RT GI nor an environment; with RT GI the walls are lit by direct light and its one bounce only, as in the path tracer, which has no such term. The whole frame darkens where it was flat-filled. The white non-metal spheres and the back panel lose the flat fill and take only the room's bounce; max_abs 148 on 97.4% of pixels (rmse 56.5), looked at before the update.

scenes.name: khronos_flight_helmet_deferred
scenes._note: Khronos validation pack: glTF-Sample-Models FlightHelmet (CC0, Microsoft), 6 meshes, 6 materials with packed occlusion-roughness-metal maps (the occlusionTexture is the metallicRoughness image: uploaded once, AO from its R), normal maps, framed by model_viewer. Exact. Known: LensesMat is alphaMode BLEND and the frame has no alpha path, so the goggle lenses render opaque. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (environment reflections): the deferred frame's environment light is split-sum IBL from a GGX-prefiltered environment (6 levels, read at the pixel's roughness) and a cosine-convolved irradiance image, scaled by the environment's intensity, weighted by RT GI's environment visibility (the fraction of GI rays that leave the scene) with GI's bounce radiance for the occluded rest, and occluded by material AO and SSAO through a specular-occlusion term; the unprefiltered mip-0 lookup, the 1x1 BRDF-LUT fallback and the metal ambient floor are gone. The leather, wood and fabric lose the mirror sheen the unprefiltered lookup gave every rough surface; max_abs 223 on 95.0% of pixels (rmse 69.6), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (SSR composition): screen-space reflections replace the environment/GI reflection where their trace hits instead of being added on top of it in tonemapping (lighting writes its environment specular E and reflection weight W, the split sum with specular occlusion, and SSR's resolve does lit += W*(c*L) - c*E before bloom and TAA, so reflected light is counted once and under one weight), and the constant ambient term is diffuse only (albedo * (1 - metallic): on metals it was a flat F0-tinted glow the path tracer has no counterpart for). The brass plaque, a smooth metal facing the room's open front, now reflects the dark environment behind the camera (its yellow was the ambient glow); max_abs 151 on 10.3% of pixels (rmse 9.2), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-26 (ambient kill): the constant ambient (0.35 x diffuse albedo, on every surface on top of RT GI) is now only the fallback of a frame with neither RT GI nor an environment; with RT GI the walls are lit by direct light and its one bounce only, as in the path tracer, which has no such term. The whole frame darkens where it was flat-filled. The room's walls and the stand darker, GI noise visible on the walls; max_abs 138 on 98.1% of pixels (rmse 50.5), looked at before the update.

scenes.name: cli_khronos_sponza_deferred
scenes._note: Khronos validation pack: glTF-Sample-Models Sponza (Crytek / Frank Meinl, PBR textures by Alexandre Pestana; see assets/khronos/Sponza/LICENSE.md), 103 meshes, 25 materials, at its own scale (about 30 m long) with a hand-placed camera in the atrium looking down the nave, a sun through the open roof and five atrium point lights; no example twin (model_viewer would frame it from outside). Exact. Known: three materials are alphaMode MASK (the potted plants' leaves among them) and the frame has no alpha test, so their cut-out leaves render as opaque cards. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (environment reflections): the deferred frame's environment light is split-sum IBL from a GGX-prefiltered environment (6 levels, read at the pixel's roughness) and a cosine-convolved irradiance image, scaled by the environment's intensity, weighted by RT GI's environment visibility (the fraction of GI rays that leave the scene) with GI's bounce radiance for the occluded rest, and occluded by material AO and SSAO through a specular-occlusion term; the unprefiltered mip-0 lookup, the 1x1 BRDF-LUT fallback and the metal ambient floor are gone. The atrium's stone and fabric lose the false sparkle of sharp sky reflections and its interior takes the sky only where GI rays reach it; max_abs 226 on 100% of pixels (rmse 28.8), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-25 (SSR composition): screen-space reflections replace the environment/GI reflection where their trace hits instead of being added on top of it in tonemapping (lighting writes its environment specular E and reflection weight W, the split sum with specular occlusion, and SSR's resolve does lit += W*(c*L) - c*E before bloom and TAA, so reflected light is counted once and under one weight), and the constant ambient term is diffuse only (albedo * (1 - metallic): on metals it was a flat F0-tinted glow the path tracer has no counterpart for). Metallic trim darker, reflections where the trace hits replacing the environment's; max_abs 150 on 47.7% of pixels (rmse 15.2), looked at before the update. Re-captured 2026-10-26 (ambient kill): the constant ambient (0.35 x diffuse albedo, on every surface on top of RT GI) is now only the fallback of a frame with neither RT GI nor an environment; with RT GI the walls are lit by direct light and its one bounce only, as in the path tracer, which has no such term. The whole frame darkens where it was flat-filled. Shadowed stone darker, lit by the sun's bounce only; max_abs 89 on 99.9% of pixels (rmse 19.3), looked at before the update.
